summary: Chubu Centrair International Airport (NGO/RJGG) opened in 2005 on a man-made island in Ise Bay off Tokoname, Aichi Prefecture. It serves the Nagoya and broader Chubu region with a single integrated terminal, a direct Meitetsu rail link, and the landside Sky Town shopping and dining complex. Its island location allows 24-hour operations and reduces noise impact on nearby communities.
faqs:
Q: How do I get from Chubu Centrair to Nagoya Station?
A: The Meitetsu Airport Line is the fastest option: μ-SKY limited express takes about 28 minutes, and regular express trains take about 37 minutes.

Q: Is there a hotel at the airport?
A: Yes, hotels are located in or adjacent to Sky Town, including Comfort Hotel Central International Airport, and are within walking distance of the terminal.

Q: Can I store luggage at the airport?
A: Yes, coin lockers and staffed baggage storage/porters are available in the terminal; locations and hours may vary, so check signs on arrival.

Q: Is there anything to do before security?
A: Yes, Sky Town offers shops, restaurants, an observation deck, and the Fu no Yu hot bath, all accessible landside before departure.
transport_tips: The Meitetsu Airport Line connects the terminal directly to Nagoya Station in about 28–37 minutes; μ-SKY trains require a reserved-seat ticket in addition to the base fare. Highway and limousine buses serve Nagoya, Kyoto, and other regional destinations, while taxis are convenient but expensive. If coming from Mie Prefecture, check the high-speed ferry to Tsu, which can be faster than road or rail depending on your destination.
local_tip: Frequent visitors buy the Meitetsu μ-SKY reserved-seat ticket from the vending machines or ticket office rather than relying on an IC card alone, then allow time to visit Sky Town and the Fu no Yu hot bath before security—it's a uniquely Japanese airport experience.
